memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"Anyone who eats the fat of an animal from which a food offering may be presented to the LORD must be cut off from their people. And wherever you live, you must not eat the blood of any bird or animal. Anyone who eats blood must be cut off from their people."'" - Lev 7:25-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Twice more the prohibition on blood, and this one reaches everywhere: wherever you live.

Leviticus later gives the reason plainly: the life of a creature is in the blood, and I have given it to you to make atonement for yourselves on the altar (Lev 17:11). Blood represented life, and life belonged to God alone. It was too significant to be treated as food.

So every meal in Israel carried a silent testimony. Life is sacred. It is not ours to consume. It belongs to the One who gave it.

Then think about what Jesus said in Capernaum, and how shocking it must have sounded: Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life (Jn 6:54). To a Jewish audience raised on this very law, the words were almost unbearable. Many of his disciples turned back and no longer followed him (Jn 6:66).

He was speaking of receiving Him by faith, not of literal consumption. But the shock was intentional. The very thing Israel was forbidden to touch, He offers freely — because His life, poured out, is what gives life to us.

Israel could never take life. Christ gives His.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I treat human life — including my own — as sacred and belonging to God?
2. What does it mean to me that Christ freely gives what Israel could never take?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You taught Israel that life belongs to You alone. Thank You that Your Son poured out His life so that I might live. Amen.
